title: Microarchitectural comparison and in-core modeling of state-of-the-art CPUs: Grace, Sapphire Rapids, and Genoa
problem: Accurately modeling and comparing the in-core performance characteristics of modern CPUs from different vendors with distinct microarchitectures. Understanding how features like write-allocate evasion are implemented differently across Zen 4, Golden Cove, and Neoverse V2.
motivation: With AMD, Intel, and Nvidia all competing in HPC, understanding the performance characteristics and microarchitectural differences of their state-of-the-art CPUs is essential for optimization and procurement decisions.
method: The authors extend the Open Source Architecture Code Analyzer (OSACA) tool to support Zen 4, Golden Cove, and Neoverse V2 microarchitectures and compare it with LLVM-MCA. They perform detailed microarchitectural analysis starting from single-core characteristics, then extend to full-node capabilities using microbenchmarks, with special focus on write-allocate evasion implementations.
key_novelty: Detailed comparative analysis of write-allocate evasion feature implementations across three different CPU vendors, revealing architectural differences and optimization opportunities specific to each microarchitecture.
contributions: Extended OSACA tool with support for Zen 4, Golden Cove, and Neoverse V2 microarchitectures
Accurate in-core performance models for Grace, Sapphire Rapids, and Genoa CPUs
Comparative analysis of write-allocate evasion implementations across vendors
Microarchitectural characterization including single-core and full-node performance capabilities

metrics.other: memory traffic reduction from write-allocate evasion

primary_theme: microarchitectural performance modeling and cross-vendor comparison
